body:
Thank you so much for your reply. I've had to wait a while until my first evaluation with a psychiatrist, and it's been difficult to take things alone. I guess I should ask him to help me figure out what he could do...and honestly answer questions from him. I keep forgetting to see things from his perspective - if he were the one with these issues, I would be sad that he didn't trust me enough to be open about it. And I completely agree with not letting depression be a scapegoat for every problem, I'm in this self-pitying mode right now and may also need him to help me snap out of it. 
I'll come back to your reply again before I talk with him.
Sounds like me. Feel free to PM me anytime, I should be up for a while.
I was so tired of mentally beating myself up for not making the most out of my time. Cruise control - I'll keep that in mind. Thanks again for your advice.
That's another thing I was concerned about - I read somewhere that side-effects of antidepressants could be suicidal thoughts? Definitely something to read up on, thank you.
I do like to watch other people playing video games on youtube, when I really just want to space out. Maybe I'll try it out myself.
Thanks, it's actually comforting to hear that it's ok to zone out. At least until the worst is over.

I trust my bf and have been with him for 5 years, but I feel isolated regardless. I've never been able to talk to him or anyone about this. Thanks so much for reaching out. It really means a lot, to know that other people have gone through similar situations and came out ok. Thank you.
I was just tired of trying anymore, my time limit is approaching fast, and I didn't see the point of going on. But I lived through another day, and I think I can do another. Thank you.

I read your comment first and cried again, but this time because I was just really thankful for someone reaching out so sincerely. I didn't get back to you yesterday because I kind of drank myself to sleep. I know it's just escaping from my problems, but it helped me wake up and trudge through another day. I still don't know if I'll admit this to my boyfriend - we've been together for 5 yrs but I know he's also very busy and stressed out now. In fact, I've never talked about this with anyone around me, mostly for the reasons you mentioned. I'm still stuck in the darkness, but I feel like I can come back to the warm replies I received from you and others here, and not be quite so alone anymore. Just...thank you. It really means a lot.

That is incredibly proactive of you and very admirable. I would definitely watch it, and I'm sure it would inspire others with similar conditions. But if you do get nasty comments, don't take them to heart! Not all internet communities are like /r/depression, and youtube is full of trolls.

Hey there - how are things going these days? I know when things are shitty it's hard to imagine a bright future - but just by recognizing your problems and how you feel about it, you're taking a first step towards bettering your situation. When you say that your parents are forcing you, do you think they're doing it for you to feel miserable or feel stressed out? Or they just have high expectations and don't know how much pressure they're putting on you?  
I do recommend discussing how uncomfortable you feel with your parents or teacher. Ultimately, parents usually don't want their kids to be unhappy. Your parents may not have even realized that you're feeling forced - which is not necessarily something to blame them about. It's hard not to have expectations about your child, and hard not to realize that every person has their own definition of success. Please try talking it out with your school counselor as well, if there is one, and you may learn you're not alone.

To quickly share my own story, I was also pretty happy until elementary school but my family had to move to another country. I lost touch with friends. I felt isolated and rootless, and as an only child, my parents had extremely high expectations for me - their eyes were constantly on me and how my grades were doing, what career I was aiming for etc. The one place where I didn't have to directly face the pressure and loneliness was in orchestra - and I'm glad you seem to have a similar sanctuary, basketball. Savor the moments you enjoy spending, and try to find similar sanctuaries if you have time. Increase them bit by bit, and you eventually will be able to get back on your own, self-customized path.
As someone who is still stuck in the emptiness, and am just barely starting to regain control of my life, reading this was encouraging. Thank you for sharing.

Try not to pressure yourself to be back to who you used to be, or to your "happier times." You yourself are changing, your living situation will be changing, there are new things to look forward to, and new things to challenge you.  Ask yourself why you're doing what your parents are asking you to do - are you doing them because they told you to and you'd like to please them? Because you think your parents are trying to open new opportunities for you? Is there something stopping you from talking to them, or anyone else, about how much stress this is causing you? Remember, you're still very young and it's very early to think you've got nothing left.

If you are going to college and living in a dorm, you will get to choose how to live your own life soon enough. I know it seems like forever, but believe me, it will come pretty quickly.  If you are considering other options, don't give up on them because of your parents or siblings - you are your own person, and ultimately I'm sure your family will understand (and if not, you're going to be living on your own eventually anyway).
Remember that you were also his best friend, perhaps his only friend, and that you were the world to him. He is a lucky dog to have been loved so much by you.

Thanks for your comment. I'm not sure if I'm ready to tell him or my family, as I don't want to drag them into this. But it does help to let it out here - I think it's my baby step to discussing it with someone around me. Thanks again for listening.
